arch.feature.name: CPU architectures
arch.feature.desc: Architecture families (x86, RISC, ARM, RISC-V and others) are researched in the shared lab, chosen in the CPU designer, and affect performance, project cost and the market rating by segment.
arch.param.ratingStrength.tip: How much the deviation of an architecture's rating multiplier from 1 is amplified or reduced. 100% is the standard effect, 0% means architectures do not affect the rating.
arch.param.notifications.tip: Show notifications: an architecture research finished or was paused, the lab went back to a technology.
arch.hub.title: CPU architectures
arch.family.proprietary.name: Proprietary ISA
arch.family.proprietary.desc: The company's own instruction set. Available from the start with no segment restrictions, but between 1985 and 1995 it loses appeal in the consumer segments.
arch.family.x86.name: x86
arch.family.x86.desc: The mass-market instruction set of personal computers. A little faster and hungrier than a proprietary ISA, at home in the high-end, mid-range and low-end segments.
arch.family.risc.name: RISC
arch.family.risc.desc: A family of simplified instruction sets (MIPS, PowerPC, SPARC). High performance per clock and moderate power draw, strong in the high-end segment and in industry.
arch.family.arm.name: ARM
arch.family.arm.desc: An energy-efficient instruction set for embedded and mobile devices. Modest performance, but low power draw and cheap development, the leader in industry.
arch.family.x86_64.name: x86-64
arch.family.x86_64.desc: The 64-bit extension of x86. Requires researched x86, adds performance and appeals most in the high-end and mid-range segments.
arch.family.arm64.name: ARM64
arch.family.arm64.desc: The 64-bit ARM architecture. Requires researched ARM, combines low power draw with good performance in the low-end segment and in industry.
arch.family.riscv.name: RISC-V
arch.family.riscv.desc: An open instruction set with no licence fees. Cheap development and low power draw, best suited to industry.
arch.designer.label: Architecture
arch.designer.tip: The architecture family the CPU is designed on. The list shows the researched families; the choice is remembered and changes IPC, power draw and the project cost.
arch.notify.pausedDefault: Research of architecture "{0}" paused: the company is in default
arch.lab.returned: The lab is back to researching "{0}"
arch.lab.pausedTech: Research of the architecture "{0}" is paused: the lab is busy with the technology "{1}"
arch.designer.ratingTip: How much the chosen architecture changes the rating of the CPU in the market segments this year (the architecture's own share, without other mods). HE is the high-end segment, MR mid-range, LE low-end, Ind industry.
arch.mods.title: Architectures
arch.mods.ipc: IPC and IPS of new CPUs ({0})
arch.pause.technology: the lab is busy with a technology
arch.tab.title: Architectures
arch.window.title: CPU architectures
arch.hub.intro: The architecture families, the shared lab and the state of the research are in the architectures window.
arch.hub.openTab: Open the tab in the research tree
arch.panel.hint: Architectures are researched in the shared lab together with the technologies: while an architecture is being researched, the technology stands still. The family for a new CPU is chosen in the designer.
arch.panel.error: The architectures panel could not be built, see Player.log for details.
arch.lab.tech: The lab is busy with the technology "{0}"
arch.lab.arch: The lab is busy with the architecture "{0}"
arch.lab.fundingTip: The share of full research funding: 1 to 100% (up to 500% with the innovation effort on). The higher it is, the faster the research goes and the more it costs per month.
arch.lab.confirm.title: Stop the technology?
arch.lab.confirm: The lab is busy with the technology "{0}". Stop it (its progress is kept) and start researching the architecture "{1}"? When the architecture is researched or stopped, the lab goes back to the technology.
arch.support.title: Software support
arch.support.hint: Software support (compilers, operating systems, developer deals) climbs towards the level your funding sets and falls without it. It decides how well your processors rate on the market. A new level takes effect from next month.
arch.support.tierTip: The funding level of the support: the higher it is, the faster the support grows and the more it costs to keep. Takes effect from next month.
arch.support.tip.tier: Tier "{0}": support heads for {1}, covering {2}% of the way each month.
arch.support.tip.off: Without funding the support falls by {0}% a month.
arch.support.tip.cap: Support for this architecture cannot rise above {0}.
arch.support.tip.free: Upkeep: none while the tier is off.
arch.designer.immatureTip: The tools of an architecture new to the company are not polished yet: for 12 months after the research a CPU project on it costs more, and the surcharge melts away month by month.
arch.designer.extTip: Multicore and SMT show their full effect on the market only with enough software support for the architecture. While it is short, the rating of such a CPU is lower. The support is set in the architectures window.
arch.techtip.ext: Software support: {0} unlocks at architecture support ≥ {1}; with no support at all the rating of such CPUs is multiplied by ×{2} (yours now: {3} — {4})
arch.eco.title: Architecture ecosystem
arch.eco.hint: The share of an architecture in CPU sales over the last 12 months, market and contracts together. The bigger it is, the more software and buyers: the rating of CPUs is multiplied by {0} + {1} × √share.
arch.eco.empty: Nothing was sold in the last 12 months: the whole ecosystem belongs to the proprietary ISA for now.
arch.royalty.title: x86 royalty
arch.royalty.free: x86 royalty: none, the licence was revoked
arch.royalty.tip: Companies without an x86 licence pay {0}% of the income of their x86 CPUs for the last full month to the licence holders, in equal parts. The player and the rivals pay the same. The sum shown is the last month's.
arch.rivals.title: Rivals
arch.rivals.hint: The architecture the competitors design on and what they research — no more than the inspector of the game shows.
arch.mail.eco.subject: {0} ecosystem passed {1}%
arch.mail.eco.body: The share of the "{0}" architecture in CPU sales over the last 12 months passed {1}%. The market now: {2}.

arch.card.tip.strength: Strength of the effect in the hub: {0}%, the market gets {1}.
arch.card.tip.assumed: The family is not researched: the support is taken as the starting one, {0} out of 100.
